source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 9ης Μαΐου — «Όσιος Ιερώνυμος ο Σιμωνοπετρίτης»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 9 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», and the head line «(1871 - 1957)» and the opening sentence — born at the village of Reiz-Dere in the district of Krini in Asia Minor in 1871, of poor and pious parents, Nikolaos Diakogiorgis and Maria — are the same man as the folder's, whose Romanian life gives «Ioan Diakoghorghis, s-a născut în anul 1871, la Reiz-Dere din Asia Mică». **The two calendars keep him on two different days and both are recorded**: the Romanian row is 7 January, which doxologia gives as the day of his repose, «pe 7 ianuarie 1957 (ajunul Sărbătorii Nașterii Domnului, după calendarul vechi)», and the Greek keeps him on 9 Μαΐου. Nothing about the Romanian row changes, and the Greek row records the day page read. **`dates` are not touched**: the folder already has 1871 and 1957 off doxologia and the Greek head line agrees with both. **What is added from the Greek is the childhood the Romanian life did not give**: the village five kilometres north-east of Alatsata and two and a half from the sea, whose people were farmers and vine-growers come from Crete and the Peloponnese; the baptismal name John; his standing as a pupil, so that his teacher sent him to teach in a nearby town as soon as he had finished the elementary school; the church that became the centre of his life; two healings by Saint Demetrius, for pains in his legs and for chickenpox, with forty days' fasting in that saint's church each time; his knowing the Salutations of the Mother of God by heart from the age of seven; and the monastic names of his family — his mother Melane, his brother Maximos, his three sisters Magdalene, Melane and Kassiane. **This reader did not read the whole page.** It is very long and `elbody.mjs` cut some forty-three thousand characters out of its middle, so the years between his youth and his repose are not recorded here from the Greek at all; nothing is claimed about them. The page also lists an Ἀκολουθία of his and the patriarchal act of his canonisation, which were not opened.
Not checked: pravoslavno.rs and the Ohrid Prologue for the corresponding Julian day (19 September 2026).
